| Images and PDF: file and app icons | NSWorkspace icon(forFile:), NSImage named icons | springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs, docs/bifrost-ui.md (widgets::folder_icon) | Partial | procedural folder icon only; no per-file-type icon set |
| Drawing: 2D drawing context and basic shapes | NSGraphicsContext, NSRectFill, NSBezierPath fill/stroke of rects and rounded rects | springboard/render/src/gfx.rs (Surface, fill_rrect, rrect_coverage, Damage) | Partial | software Surface with rect, rounded rect, squircle masks and damage tracking; no general path object, no clipping paths, no affine transform stack for apps |
| Drawing: Bezier paths, gradients, shadows | NSBezierPath, NSGradient, NSShadow | springboard/render/src/bezier.rs, springboard/render/src/gradient.rs | Partial | Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. gradients exist only inside specific widgets (folder icon); no public path, gradient or shadow objects |
| Drawing: materials and vibrancy | NSVisualEffectView, Liquid Glass | springboard/render/src/glass.rs, springboard/render/src/appearance.rs | Partial | glass hook and light/dark cross-fade exist; Spotlight blur still missing per CLAUDE.md |
| Drawing: view-level drawing and redraw | NSView draw(_:), needsDisplay, NSCell drawing | springboard/sdk/src/view/ | Partial | retained views with damage rects; not the NSView draw cycle or NSCell model |

n/a · coverage 44% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corefoundation) · REA `ev_20f07fbb6a8d75acd01162d9b322abeab9e8d8032ed51aa75f429dd312523baa`

Core Foundation is the C ABI layer (CFTypeRef, opaque CF* types, CFAllocator, run loops, sockets, plug-ins) that Apple bridges to Foundation. BifrOSt is Rust and has no C ABI requirement, so the CF types themselves are n/a. The Foundation-level behaviour they back (preferences, notifications, main queue, URLs, locale, formatting, plists) has partial counterparts in the Foundation batches.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Preferences (CFPreferences) | Preferences Utilities, CFPreferences keys and domains | springboard/sdk/src/defaults.rs (UserDefaults, typed values, atomic per-app file) | Partial | Per-app typed defaults exist; no shared cross-app domains or CFPreferences-style host-wide keys |
| Notification center (CFNotificationCenter) | CFNotificationCenter, CFNotificationCenterGetLocalCenter | springboard/sdk/src/notification.rs (NotificationCenter add_observer, post, remove_observer; DistributedNotificationCenter) | Partial | Observer add, post and remove exist; the object argument is a u64 handle, not an arbitrary object reference |
| Run loop and timers (CFRunLoop, CFRunLoopTimer, CFRunLoopSource, CFRunLoopObserver) | CFRunLoop, CFRunLoopTimer, CFRunLoopSource, CFRunLoopObserver | springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs (DispatchQueue main, async_after, drain_main, wake fd) | Partial | Main-queue dispatch and delayed work exist; no run-loop modes, observers or custom input sources |
| URL access utilities (CFURL) | CFURL, Core Foundation URL Access Utilities, CFURLEnumerator | springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (URLRequest, HTTPURLResponse, URLCache) | Partial | Network requests and cache exist; no CFURL path, resource-value or enumerator API |
| Locale and time zone (CFLocale, CFTimeZone, CFCalendar) | CFLocale, CFTimeZone, CFCalendar, CFDate | springboard/sdk/src/locale.rs (Locale identifier, separators, language) | Partial | Locale identifier and number separators exist; no time zone or calendar API in the SDK |
| Number and date formatters (CFNumberFormatter, CFDateFormatter) | CFNumberFormatter, CFDateFormatter | springboard/ui/src/format.rs (byte_count, duration, relative, grouped) | Partial | Fixed helper formats only; no general formatter objects with locale-aware patterns |
| Property lists and Codable-style encoding (CFPropertyList, CFXMLParser) | CFPropertyList, CFXMLParser, CFXMLTree, CFXMLNode | springboard/sdk/src/coding.rs (encode/decode, field, ISO 8601 format and parse) | Partial | Two encoders and a decoder exist; no XML property-list parser API for apps |
| Attributed strings (CFAttributedString) | CFAttributedString, CFMutableAttributedString | springboard/sdk/src/attributed.rs | Partial | Rich text container exists; CF statistical writing-direction call has no counterpart |

Gaps: No CFPreferences-style host-wide or cross-app preference domains (springboard/sdk/src/defaults.rs is per app).; No CFURL path, resource-value or enumerator API (springboard/sdk/src/url.rs covers network requests only).; No time zone or calendar API in the SDK (springboard/sdk/src/locale.rs has identifier and separators only).; No general locale-aware number or date formatter objects (springboard/ui/src/format.rs has fixed helpers).; No app-facing plug-in or bundle resource lookup (CFPlugIn, CFBundle)..

Apple's Distributed framework is the Swift distributed actor model (actor systems, typed remote calls, local test system). BifrOSt has no actor system or typed remote-call encoder; its closest pieces are a cross-app broadcast (DistributedNotificationCenter) and a per-app JSON-RPC control socket, which cover the message-passing side but not location-transparent actor references.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Remote call targets and invocation encoding | RemoteCallTarget, RemoteCallArgument, DistributedTargetInvocationEncoder, DistributedTargetInvocationDecoder, DistributedTargetInvocationResultHandler | springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (handle_line, handle_line_ex, encode) | Partial | JSON-RPC method dispatch with method names and JSON params exists; no typed invocation encoder/decoder, no target identifiers, no result-handler protocol |
| Cross-process broadcast messages | Distributed notifications (NSDistributedNotificationCenter-style delivery; Distributed framework docs do not cover it directly) | springboard/sdk/src/notification.rs (DistributedNotificationCenter, post_with, add_observer); springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs:822 (ToShell::DistPost relay); docs/bifrost-ui.md:1219 | Partial | shell relays posts to every running app; user_info is string to string, max 32 entries and 1024 characters a value; no suspensionBehavior, no deliverImmediately; plain post stays process-local |
| Remote call errors | DistributedActorCodingError, DistributedActorSystemError, ExecuteDistributedTargetError | springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (RpcError, METHOD_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PARAMS, INTERNAL_ERROR, TIMEOUT) | Partial | JSON-RPC error codes cover method, params and timeout failures; no coding error type for typed arguments |
| Local testing actor system | LocalTestingDistributedActorSystem and its ActorID, Address, invocation encoder/decoder types | springboard/sdk/src/distributed.rs | Partial | Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. an in-process RPC test double for control methods would be the equivalent; none exists |
| Agent and tool access to running apps | No direct Distributed counterpart (remote invocation across processes) | springboard/mcp/src/ (agent MCP server); tools/app-control.py; tools/pi-bifrost-control/client.ts | OS only | agents reach the desktop and apps through MCP and per-app control sockets, not through a shared invocation layer apps can call |

Gaps: No location-transparent remote actor references or actor system; no SDK type for a remote handle to another app's object; No typed remote-call encoder or decoder: control methods pass untyped JSON params and results; No local test double for cross-process calls (LocalTestingDistributedActorSystem equivalent); Cross-app notifications are string-to-string only, capped at 32 entries and 1024 characters per value; Cross-app notifications have no suspensionBehavior: an app that is not running misses the post.

<a id="observation"></a>
### Observation

Partial · coverage 42% · macOS 14.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/observation) · REA `ev_59ddd532abf1677b1e3304c8d7443c1ffaef9a4e65513f0e7e8dd952321415d0`

BifrOSt has manual value observation: an Observable<T> that notifies subscribers only when the value changes, with Combine-style sink, map and remove_duplicates. A set made inside a subscriber is queued and delivered in order, and cancelling a subscriber during a change sticks. with_observation_tracking records the observables a closure reads and fires one on-change callback; Observable::observations pulls changes in order. It still has no @Observable macro, no tracking options or tokens, no continuous observation, and no async sequence.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Observable conformance (@Observable macro) | Observable() macro, Observable protocol | none (Rust; no macro) | Gap | No per-type macro that synthesizes change notification for every stored property. Observable<T> wraps one whole value, not a model object's properties. |
| Change notification on value change | Observable protocol, ObservationRegistrar | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Observable::set, update, subscribe, sink); springboard/ui/src/observe.rs (Observable<T>::set, subscribe(old, new)) | Partial | Notifies only when the value differs (PartialEq) in the UI-model copy; the SDK copy notifies on every set. A set made from inside a subscriber is queued and delivered after the running change, in order (fixed in SDK, was dropped). Cancelling another subscriber during a change is now durable. UI-model copy (ui/src/observe.rs) is unchanged: its subscribers receive old and new values only. |
| Automatic dependency tracking | withObservationTracking(_:onChange:), withObservationTracking(options:_:onChange:) | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (with_observation_tracking, Observable::get records reads) | Partial | with_observation_tracking(apply, on_change) records each Observable read by get() inside apply and calls on_change once when one changes; the tracking then ends. Apple's withObservationTracking returns only the closure value and also covers options, and its onChange runs before the change; here on_change runs after the change, and reads inside on_change are not tracked. Only the SDK Observable is tracked; the UI-model copy is not. |
| Async change sequence | Observations, withContinuousObservation(options:apply:) | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Observable::observations, Observations::try_next, pending_len) | Partial | Pull-based sequence of the changes after the call, oldest first; dropping it stops recording. It is the synchronous counterpart of Apple's Observations: it has no suspension, no AsyncSequence conformance and no withContinuousObservation(options:apply:). |
| Observation tracking options and tokens | ObservationTracking, ObservationTracking.Options, ObservationTracking.Token, ObservationTracking.Event | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Subscription, Cancellables) | Partial | Subscription cancels on drop (AnyCancellable). No event or options types for tracking. |
| Ignore or track individual properties | ObservationIgnored(), ObservationTracked() | n/a | n/a | Macro-only behaviour of the Swift language; with no macro in BifrOSt there is nothing to mark. |
| Notifications from system state | Observation Registrar for model state (manual) | springboard/sdk/src/process_info.rs (observe_thermal_state, observe_low_power_mode); docs/bifrost-ui.md:1214 (NotificationCenter add_observer, post); docs/bifrost-ui.md:1542 (workspace observe) | Partial | Observer-style subscriptions exist for system events (NotificationCenter, workspace, thermal state, Low Power Mode). They are not Observation's property-level tracking. |

Gaps: No @Observable macro equivalent: each Observable must be wired by hand, and with_observation_tracking tracks only SDK Observable reads.; No withContinuousObservation(options:apply:), ObservationTracking.Options, Event or Token: with_observation_tracking is one-shot and returns only the closure value.; Observations is pull-based (try_next), not an AsyncSequence; there is no executor or suspension in the pure std model.; docs/bifrost-ui.md:1435 still describes the old re-entrant set limit; that shared doc is out of scope for this change and is listed for a later update.; SwiftUI-style integration (view invalidation from observed model state) not verified in code; no binding found in this pass..

<a id="permissionkit"></a>
### PermissionKit

OS only · coverage 42% · macOS 26.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/permissionkit) · REA `ev_cd9fa96eaa8c651fdce9299018cdf03ab50f910d59b0e3e092d23a839bec79fe`

PermissionKit lets an app ask a child's parent or guardian for a communication or app-update exception through a system UI. BifrOSt has no app-facing equivalent: the system layer enforces Screen Time limits and Downtime, and no SDK module lets an app send a permission question to a parent or receive the answer.

Partial · coverage 39% · macOS 14.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/symbols) · REA `ev_4228c223ea1ec28dfa7061baa7d6168c30cb9d1b86003c9d7dcf0cab875728f3`

The Symbols framework is Apple's set of universal symbol effects (appear, bounce, pulse, variableColor, replace and others) for SF Symbols images in AppKit, UIKit and SwiftUI. BifrOSt has a fixed set of 59 hand-drawn line glyphs named after SF Symbols and a generic implicit animation system, but no symbol-effect API and no symbol layers or rendering modes, so none of the effects can be applied to a symbol image.

Not the SF Symbols catalogue. The renderer's symbol font path finds no real symbol font on the device, so the drawings are what ships |
| Appear, disappear and scale effects | appear, disappear, scale (AppearSymbolEffect, DisappearSymbolEffect, ScaleSymbolEffect) | springboard/ui/src/symbol_effect.rs, springboard/sdk/src/glyphs.rs (glyph_effect) | Partial | Wave 2 (symbols, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no SDK type or call applies a symbol effect to a glyph; glyphs are drawn once per frame with no per-layer state |
| Bounce and pulse effects | bounce, pulse (BounceSymbolEffect, PulseSymbolEffect) | springboard/ui/src/symbol_effect.rs | Partial | Wave 2 (symbols, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. the bounce spring and dock bounce are fixed motions for scrolling and the dock, not symbol effects an app can request |
| Variable color effect | variableColor (VariableColorSymbolEffect) | none | Gap | no variable layers in glyphs.rs; each glyph is one colour |
| Content transitions (replace, automatic) | replace, automatic (ReplaceSymbolEffect, AutomaticSymbolEffect, ContentTransitionSymbolEffect) | springboard/ui/src/symbol_effect.rs (replace_poses | Partial | Wave 2 (symbols, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. an app swapping one glyph for another gets a plain redraw, not a per-layer replace animation; implicit animation cannot tell a glyph change apart from any other opacity change |
| Discrete and indefinite effect protocols and options | SymbolEffect, DiscreteSymbolEffect, IndefiniteSymbolEffect, TransitionSymbolEffect, SymbolEffectOptions | springboard/ui/src/symbol_effect.rs (SymbolEffect | Partial | Wave 2 (symbols, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no effect trait, no repeat or speed options, and no way to start or stop a looping effect on a glyph |

BifrOSt has no object graph, managed object context, fetch request or persistent store layer. ### Core ML

Partial · coverage 41% · macOS 10.13 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml) · REA `ev_61bb5baae834f9b3d498207c8aefac9606a9eefacd2c879fbc0c612a09006428`

Core ML runs trained models on the device (MLModel, feature providers, tensors, compute-device policy, on-device updates). BifrOSt has no model loading, inference, tensor or feature-provider API, and no SDK module for it. The keyboard predictor is a hand-built word-frequency trie, and the Assistant app calls a remote Messages API, so neither is an on-device model.

Apple's framework is an out-of-process app extension that lets a developer inspect a crashed app (reason, binary images, symbolication, a read-only corpse port) and send its own report. BifrOSt captures crashes at the system level only: the shell's panic hook and the Linux coredump list. No app-facing SDK API inspects another crashed process or builds a report from it.

No app extension mechanism lets an app's own code run when another app crashes. Apple's handler runs out of process; BifrOSt has no equivalent hook. |
| Crash reason (CrashedProcess.reason, CrashReason) | CrashedProcess.reason, CrashReason | springboard/src/shell/diag.rs (CrashEntry signature, from crash.log); springboard/apps/console-desktop/src/model.rs (parse_coredump_list: SIG mapped to Fault) | OS only | The reason is recorded by the shell and by systemd-coredump, but apps get it only through the Console and dev tooling, not through the SDK. |
| Binary images and symbolication (binaryImages, symbolicateAddress(es), SymbolicatedFrame) | CrashedProcess.binaryImages, BinaryImageInfo, symbolicateAddress(_:), symbolicateAddresses(_:), symbolAddress(imageName:symbolName:) | springboard/sdk/src/crash_report.rs | Partial | Wave 3 (theme-14, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Symbolication is done by hand (coredumpctl and gdb, per the diagnose-crash skill). No SDK call maps addresses to symbols inside another process. |
| Corpse port (corpsePort, read-only Mach port) | CrashedProcess.corpsePort | none | n/a | Mach ports are an Apple kernel mechanism. The Linux equivalent is the core file, which is not exposed to apps. |

Apple's TabularData is a typed data-frame library for preparing machine-learning training tables (DataFrame, typed columns, statistical summaries, CSV/JSON import and export). BifrOSt has no data-frame or typed-column type and no statistics layer; the only table-like pieces are the UI table's sort model, a JSON Codable layer and an ad hoc CSV parser inside the weather widget. <a id="app-intents-testing"></a>
### App Intents Testing

Partial · coverage 41% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintentstesting) · REA `ev_543336330e7ad0192e202bf22b580637f737f40e4078c09d8857b7cb9865c71b`

BifrOSt has an App Intents runtime served over the control socket (intent.list, intent.<id>, entity.query) and a headless UI test kit, and the intent dispatch function is public so Rust unit tests can run intents in-process. There is no intent test layer: no catalog type, no typed result or value-query result types, no entity annotation (onscreen context), and no type-erased test wrappers, so tests pass and compare raw JSON.

### Automator

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.4 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/automator) · REA `ev_92931747df2475eb5c7c1609143dbc235c17a2ebaeacf97a4e6864461e6a6ed8`

Apple's Automator is a workflow engine that runs ordered action bundles and shell or AppleScript actions, with a workflow view and controller. BifrOSt has no workflow engine and no loadable action bundles. Its closest parts are the Shortcuts app, which stores and edits ordered lists of built-in actions, and the App Intents SDK, which gives apps typed actions. Shortcuts runs nothing yet: its actions are only logged because the shell cannot receive them over the app protocol.

There is no bundle format, no install location scan (Automator loads /System/Library/Automator, /Library/Automator, ~/Library/Automator) and no view for action parameters. |

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.5 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/scriptingbridge) · REA `ev_c5d179ada5d816aa92356565b0eea84198d86fbb156b5f7d28b04153ee82c2d8`

Scripting Bridge drives other apps by sending Apple events to their sdef-described scripting interface, with generated Objective-C proxies. BifrOSt has no Apple-event or sdef layer and no generated proxies. Its nearest counterpart is a per-app JSON-RPC control socket that only the same user can reach, plus a workspace API for launching and watching apps. Apps can read and call each other's named methods, but there is no generic property and element model.

There is no handle object for a target app; a caller addresses it by app id and gets the socket path. |
| Launch and activate a target app | SBApplication activate(), launchFlags | springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (open_with, observe DidLaunchApplication and DidActivateApplication) | Partial | open_with starts an installed app by id. Launch flags and an explicit activate call are not exposed. workspace.rs states that nothing there launches a binary. |

No machine-readable dictionary and no generated client classes. Each app lists its methods at runtime (app.methods). |
| Properties and elements (get, set, property(withCode:), elementArray(withCode:)) | SBObject property(withCode:), property(with:code:), elementArray(withCode:), setTo(_:), get() | springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (method dispatch via handle(method, params)); springboard/apps/notes-desktop/CHANGELOG.md (notes.list, notes.get) | Partial | Apps expose named read methods, such as notes.list and notes.get. Nothing here sets properties. No generic object graph exists, and no property code is addressed through a shared model. |

ColorSync is the ICC profile and colour-transform engine. BifrOSt has no ICC profile loading, no profile-to-profile transforms, no device or display profiles and no HDR path. ### Game Controller

BifrOSt has no game controller API. Its evdev layer decodes touch, pointer, keyboard and key events and nothing else, so an app cannot discover a gamepad, read its buttons or sticks, or drive its haptics. The framework's keyboard and mouse profiles map loosely to the input layer that exists, but no app receives them through an SDK API.

The kernel-level hot-plug watch exists, but it only serves the recovery chord. No controller list or connect event reaches apps. |

<a id="gamekit"></a>
### GameKit (Game Center)

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamekit) · REA `ev_efdcc85c66c5d4a24f8d528b1b122fe09841b97cf6aa0fb3b9f20a909413b6ab`

GameKit is the client API for Apple's Game Center service: player identity, leaderboards, achievements, friends, matches and turn-based play. The service is Apple-hosted and BifrOSt has no Game Center or equivalent online game service, so no counterpart is planned. Local game state is covered by the Games app and the seeded-deck test pin, not by GameKit.

| Players and friends | GKPlayer, GKBasePlayer, GKLocalPlayerListener | nothing found | n/a | Friend graph lives in Apple's service. |
| Game Center dashboard and access point | GKAccessPoint, GKDialogController, GKViewController | nothing found | n/a | Apple-hosted dashboard UI. |
| Leaderboards | GKLeaderboard, GKLeaderboardSet, GKLeaderboardScore | nothing found | n/a | Server-side ranking. |
| Achievements | GKAchievement, GKAchievementDescription | nothing found | n/a | Server-side award state. |
| Real-time multiplayer matches | GKMatchRequest, GKMatchmaker, GKMatch | nothing found | n/a | Peer networking through Game Center matchmaking. No BifrOSt multiplayer transport exists. |
| Turn-based matches | GKTurnBasedMatch and related classes | nothing found | n/a | Game Center stores and forwards match data. |

Gaps: No online game service, so no leaderboards, achievements or friends. This is an Apple-service dependency, not a missing local API.; No multiplayer peer transport in the SDK..

### GameplayKit

GameplayKit is a game-logic framework: entities and components, state machines, pathfinding and agents, noise, decision and rule systems, and seeded randomness. BifrOSt has no app-facing SDK API for any of the game-logic parts. GameSave syncs an app's save files through iCloud Drive with conflict resolution, offline play and alerts. BifrOSt has no app-facing save sync: apps get a private local data directory and advisory file locks, and the games app keeps only best scores on disk. The bifrost-cloud backend stores encrypted whole-device backups, but no SDK path maps an app save directory to it.

No API returns a cloud-backed directory for an app. The app data directory is local only; nothing syncs it. |

<a id="glkit"></a>
### GLKit

Partial · coverage 44% · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/glkit) · REA `ev_2dea8330752a36acabb14ce26422118cccfeccc1eef2a1724b27913e3d95c67d`

GLKit is an OpenGL and OpenGL ES helper layer (GL view, view controller render loop, shader effects, mesh and texture loading, math). Apple marks most of it deprecated on macOS from 10.14, and macOS requires an OpenGL 3.2 Core Profile context. BifrOSt has no app-facing GL view, shader effect or mesh API; its GPU presenter is internal, and apps get blur materials, a draw and animation loop and image decoding instead.

| Render loop controller | GLKViewController (preferredFramesPerSecond, isPaused, pauseOnWillResignActive, resumeOnDidBecomeActive); iOS and tvOS only per docc, not on macOS | springboard/sdk/src/view/app.rs:216 draw(), :222 draw_at(ctx, s, t) time-based drawing; springboard/sdk/src/view/animation.rs (Timing, Transaction) | Partial | apps are redrawn by the SDK's timed draw path, with no frame-rate, pause or app-activation controls |
| Shader-based effects | GLKNamedEffect, GLKBaseEffect (lighting, transform), GLKReflectionMapEffect, GLKSkyboxEffect | none app-facing; shader sources in springboard/src/gpu/shaders.rs (layer_fragment_source, fade_fragment_source) are internal | Gap | no app-supplied shaders or lighting model |
| Effect properties | GLKEffectProperty, Fog, Light, Texture, Material, Transform | springboard/ui/src/linalg.rs, springboard/ui/src/mesh.rs, springboard/ui/src/shading.rs | Partial | Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no effect configuration objects |
| Blur and glass materials | No direct GLKit equivalent; GLKBaseEffect and GLKSkyboxEffect cover shading only | springboard/sdk/src/widgets.rs:22 Material, :297 material(), :307 visual_effect() (blur plus tint, Reduce Transparency); springboard/render/src/gfx.rs:788 glass panel | Partial | the app-facing material covers the blur-and-tint case that shader effects would otherwise be used for; no custom blur radius or shader |

Gaps: No app-facing GL view or drawable: apps cannot create an OpenGL or GLES context on BifrOSt (springboard/src/gpu/mod.rs is internal).; No shader effect classes (GLKBaseEffect and related) and no way for apps to supply shaders.; No 3D math types (matrix, vector, quaternion) in the SDK; only the browser engine's 2D transform.; No mesh or 3D buffer API.; No background GPU texture loader for apps; image decode is CPU-only (springboard/render/src/imgdec.rs).; Apple deprecated most of GLKit on macOS from 10.14. Parity work here would target the Metal-equivalent path rather than GLKit, so this framework may stay a documented n/a for new apps..

Partial · coverage 47% · macOS 10.9 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/spritekit) · REA `ev_9be83454be472ad9b63487454441d5b45d38296db93613aa7ecffa332b60902f`

SpriteKit is a 2D scene, node, action, physics, particle and tile-map framework for games. BifrOSt has no 2D scene graph, physics world, particle system, tile map or shader API for apps. Its retained view tree, property animation, timing curves and image decoding cover the general UI counterparts only; the Games app (2048, Minesweeper, Klondike) is hand-written and does not use an engine.

### Audio Toolbox

<a id="audio-unit"></a>
### Audio Unit

Partial · coverage 44% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/audiounit) · REA `ev_3bf9c005e0da939facd73989466bcbdab9f09176783e42e4aeed3b6e830276e4`

Apple's Audio Unit framework hosts third-party AU v2 and v3 plug-ins and provides the AUAudioUnit subclassing API for plug-in extensions. BifrOSt has no plug-in host and no plug-in extension API. The DAW ships its own built-in instruments and effects as JavaScript plug-in directories, which are not Audio Units. The Apple page itself marks the framework as deprecated in favour of Audio Toolbox.

<a id="avrouting"></a>
### AVRouting

Partial · coverage 38% · macOS 13.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avrouting) · REA `ev_14110f8179b556b56f5de61c07bede4c7dfac89ff255facccf244207b2b7d697`

AVRouting lets an app add third-party media receivers to the system route picker (AirPlay-style) through custom routing controllers, routing events and action items, and arbitrates playback between participants. BifrOSt has no route picker, no third-party receiver discovery and no playback arbitration API; the only routing is a local speaker/headphone switch in the audio layer.

### Core Audio

Partial · coverage 46% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudio) · REA `ev_bd10e360fb1e915d03b738fad1e0a829b4d87a74e798502bbe22e6d509ce6332`

BifrOSt covers speaker playback, microphone capture and volume through an ALSA and libasound layer owned by one audio service, and apps reach it over a socket client for playback transport and recording. The HAL object model, virtual audio drivers, aggregate devices, hardware clocks and per-process audio taps have no counterpart; no SDK exposes device objects.

<a id="core-audio-types"></a>
### Core Audio Types

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudiotypes) · REA `ev_98c7b647aeb9a63cfda5aad9fb900d0d1f51f13a1c9a5723f27315c033167e44`

Core Audio Types is a set of C data types (buffers, channel layouts, timestamps, format descriptions, SMPTE time) shared by Core Audio. BifrOSt has no shared type set for these: the media stack passes plain rate and channel counts, interleaved S16 PCM and microseconds, and keeps its format and channel handling inside each decoder. SMPTE timecode and the OSStatus error model have no counterpart.

There is no bits-per-sample, bytes-per-frame or format-flag description. |
| AudioBuffer and AudioBufferList | AudioBuffer, AudioBufferList | springboard/src/media/audiofile.rs (interleaved S16 packets); springboard/third_party/symphonia-codec-aac/src/aac/mod.rs (planar AudioBuffer<f32> inside the AAC decoder) | Partial | Buffers are a Vec or a planar decoder buffer. There is no multi-buffer list type shared with apps. |

No layout tag or per-channel label is exposed, and the layout is not carried through the audio service. |
| Codec class descriptions | AudioClassDescription | springboard/src/media/codec.rs (codec sniff from content type and first bytes) | Partial | Codec identity is an internal enum chosen by sniffing. There is no descriptor type that apps can query. |

<a id="photokit"></a>
### PhotoKit

Partial · coverage 44% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photokit) · REA `ev_c5daec50d0ec7872629a366160cc42fbfa15d118ce6fd1d0e4113eb6a3df1689`

BifrOSt has a built-in Photos app that browses a folder-based library (All Photos, Favorites, Recently Deleted, Screenshots, Recents), with thumbnails, a viewer, a slideshow, a basic editor and JPEG EXIF reading. Apps get no PhotoKit-style API: there is no shared library access, no asset fetch, no picker, no Live Photo, no editing extension and no change observation.

<a id="screen-saver"></a>
### Screen Saver

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/screensaver) · REA `ev_cc2a3e312b2679aab08837530b31bc4264f252a6ac1417506af9f1d0610ddb94`

Apple's framework is a plug-in interface: a .saver bundle subclasses ScreenSaverView, which the system animates in its own engine. BifrOSt has no such plug-in host, no SDK class for it, and no screen saver preview or configuration sheet. The idle display-off, auto-lock and suspend-after-screen-off behaviour that a screen saver sits on top of exists in the shell and system layer, but no app can hook into it.

<a id="apple-cryptokit"></a>
### Apple CryptoKit

OS only · coverage 33% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptokit) · REA `ev_daa965c42360c845f78ea59d8b10278b229b5e0289fef403e27794bb99134bc7`

BifrOSt has SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256 and ChaCha20 inside the shell, used only to protect the keychain file and to verify updates and backups. Apps get no hashing, cipher, signature, key agreement or typed key API; the SDK keychain stores opaque secret bytes. Most of CryptoKit (SHA-2 384/512, SHA-3, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519, NIST curves, HPKE, HKDF, post-quantum KEM and signatures, Secure Enclave) has no counterpart.

<a id="core-hid"></a>
### Core HID

OS only · coverage 50% · macOS 15.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehid) · REA `ev_753a243aa65ad9ea11fcc201fb9df0b957d176eca3aa12ae9d00fedf5d59ec59`

Core HID is a user-space API for discovering HID devices, reading their element values, sending reports and emulating virtual devices. BifrOSt has the kernel-side equivalent for its own shell: evdev discovery, classification of keyboards, pointers, touchscreens, power and lid devices, and a uinput keyboard for agent control. No SDK module exposes any of this to apps, and the framework's report-descriptor model is not implemented.

Discovery runs inside the shell only. No SDK API lists devices for an app; springboard/sdk/src has no HID or device module. |
| Device classification by capability | HIDDeviceTransport, HIDDeviceLocalizationCode, usage pages (HIDUsage) | springboard/ui/src/hid_match.rs (Usage::role | Partial | Wave 5 (w5-core-hid, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Roles covers touchscreen, pointer, touchpad, keyboard, power and lid from evdev bits. There are no HID usage pages and no transport or localization codes. |
| Report descriptor elements and collections | HIDElement, HIDElementCollection, HIDReportID, HIDReportType | springboard/ui/src/hid_report.rs | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. BifrOSt never parses a HID report descriptor. It consumes the kernel's evdev translation. |
| Reading element values and input reports | HIDElement.Value, HIDElementUpdate, HIDDeviceClient input callbacks | springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Decoder at line 63 turns evdev records into touch and key events) | OS only | The values stay inside the shell. Apps get key and touch events through the window system, not HID values. |
| Sending output reports to a device | HIDDeviceClient (set report, for example an LED) | springboard/ui/src/hid_report.rs | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Devices are read-only. Nothing sets LEDs, force feedback or feature reports. |

Gaps: No app-facing device manager: no SDK API lists HID devices, filters them by usage page or vendor, or reports hotplug to an app.; No report descriptor parsing (HIDElement, HIDElementCollection), so apps cannot read arbitrary HID devices such as custom controllers or instruments.; No output reports or feature reports (LED, force feedback, configuration) to devices.; No virtual HID device API for apps; the only virtual device is the agent uinput keyboard.; Transport and localization codes are not modelled..

<a id="darwin-notify"></a>
### Darwin Notify

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.14 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/darwinnotify) · REA `ev_525d60606f901be8b59a405caf5a5af1d6f7b2d77f2724156320402b56271398`

Darwin Notify is a system-wide, name-keyed notification facility with integer tokens, state values and kernel-level delivery. BifrOSt has no equivalent: the nearest app-facing counterpart is the Foundation-style DistributedNotificationCenter, which relays string-named broadcasts between running apps through the shell. System event names (time zone, mounts, clock, network) are not broadcast to apps by name.

Observer closures are tied to the main thread; no queue argument. |

| Driver registry data types | OSArray, OSDictionary, OSData, OSNumber, OSString, OSSerialization | none | n/a | IORegistry object model; BifrOSt reads sysfs directly |

<a id="execution-policy"></a>
### Execution Policy

n/a · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/executionpolicy) · REA `ev_0de80b8ab6c05378ee131c48fb040ec0a03f8539abd5fcf4a61c182a71fa8ae3`

Apple's framework lets a developer tool ask the user for an exception so that locally built software may run under the execution policy (a trust gate on code the developer built). BifrOSt has no such trust gate and no exception mechanism: every installed app launches inside a fail-closed sandbox chosen by the shell, so there is no equivalent to request or record.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Developer tool authorization (EPDeveloperTool: authorizationStatus, requestAccess(completionHandler:)) | EPDeveloperTool | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (no authorization API) | n/a | The sandbox decides what an app may touch, not whether a developer tool may be trusted. Nothing asks the user for developer-tool access, and no SDK API exposes it. |
| Execution policy exceptions (EPExecutionPolicy: addException(for:)) | EPExecutionPolicy | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs | n/a | The launch boundary is fail-closed with no exception path, as docs/app-isolation.md states (no unrestricted fallback). Adding an exception would weaken that design, so it is intentionally absent rather than missing. |
| Launch enforcement of app policy (the counterpart that gates which code runs) | ExecutionPolicy Constants (EPErrorDomain), EPError | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs; docs/app-isolation.md | OS only | Launch is refused when identity, permission validation or sandbox setup fails, and unsupported permissions fail the launch. The system layer enforces this, but apps get no SDK API to query or report the policy error domain. |
| Error reporting (EPError, EPErrorDomain) | EPError, EPErrorDomain | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs | Partial | Launch failures return io errors inside the shell. No typed, app-facing error domain exists for policy failures. |

Gaps: No app-facing API for developer-tool access requests (EPDeveloperTool); decide with the owner whether a sideload or local-build trust prompt is wanted at all, since the current design has no exception path; Policy launch failures are not exposed to apps as a typed error domain (EPError, EPErrorDomain equivalent).

Related: [Exception Handling](#exception-handling), [Security](#security), [Endpoint Security](#endpoint-security), [Core Services](#core-services), [Security Foundation](#security-foundation).

<a id="force-feedback"></a>
### Force Feedback

Partial · coverage 29% · macOS 10.2 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/forcefeedback) · REA `ev_cfcdde9a3970a00d568422cade4aaff07d84740a3b46f512a0a2d9db35042d16`

Apple's Force Feedback framework is a legacy C API (FFCreateDevice, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart) for HID force-feedback devices such as wheels and joysticks. BifrOSt has no force-feedback code path: the evdev reader does not read EV_FF capabilities or upload effects, and the SDK's haptic() call is dropped by the shell. Nothing in the framework is covered.

### GSS

Partial · coverage 46% · macOS 10.14 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gss) · REA `ev_03afbf53fe958fca77ef73ab27bde47da0f2635756db20c77c1ccb84573f0d63`

Apple's GSS framework is the GSS-API (RFC 2743/2744) for Kerberos-style authenticated sessions, message protection and name handling. BifrOSt has no GSS-API implementation, no Kerberos or krb5 code and no SDK surface for it. The only nearby work is the per-app keychain for stored passwords and Wi-Fi Enterprise (EAP) settings, which do not perform GSS security-context exchange.

### IOKit

IOKit's device-access layer exists on BifrOSt only in the Linux system layer (sysfs, /dev nodes, DRM, evdev, v4l2, ALSA control, Bluetooth), used by the shell and daemons. <a id="iousbhost"></a>
### IOUSBHost

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iousbhost) · REA `ev_a8792b7a789634fc2e35b8dfc894673ef8d9fe7860fc71b9c0e72e944432958c`

IOUSBHost is Apple's framework for user-space host-mode USB drivers that let apps talk to custom USB devices. BifrOSt has no app-facing USB transport API: the Linux kernel drives USB, and the shell and daemons handle input, camera and audio devices by class. Raw device claim, descriptors, pipes and isochronous streams have no SDK counterpart, and the app sandbox does not expose USB device nodes.

No SDK call for an app to claim a USB device or send control requests. Apps run under bwrap with no /dev/bus/usb binding (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs binds only /dev/snd and /dev/dri). |
| Interface, pipe and stream I/O (control, bulk, interrupt, isochronous) | IOUSBHostInterface, IOUSBHostPipe, IOUSBHostStream, IOUSBHostIOSource | springboard/core/src/usb_pipe.rs | Partial | Wave 4 (theme-14, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No pipe or stream abstraction exposed to apps. |
| Isochronous transfer options | IOUSBHostIsochronousTransfer*, IOUSBHostIsochronousTransaction | springboard/core/src/usb_pipe.rs | Partial | Wave 4 (theme-14, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Needed for audio and video class devices if apps are to drive them directly. |

No app SDK exposes USB properties or matching. |
| Keyboards, mice and pointing devices | IOUSBHost (HID devices via USB) | springboard/src/bare/input.rs | OS only | Input works in the shell. Apps get events through the window system, not USB descriptors. |

On Linux the kernel owns it, and a desktop app has no use for it. |

The triage note says likely n/a; the framework's stated use cases (cameras, audio, scanners, printers, MIDI, hubs) are mostly covered at the system layer, which leaves custom device drivers as the real gap..

<a id="kernel"></a>
### Kernel

n/a · coverage 50% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel) · REA `ev_04dec99a6c1f7907fcfd7ec40e64ed5108319340a7176281b72ffd17f6eb1c2a`

Kernel covers kernel extensions (kexts), the IOKit base classes for in-kernel drivers, and BSD/Mach kernel interfaces. These are specific to Apple's XNU kernel and kext loading model. BifrOSt runs on Linux, where drivers are in-tree or loaded by the Linux kernel itself, and BifrOSt ships no kernel extension or kernel-resident API for apps.

| IOKit driver base classes | IOKit Fundamentals, Hardware Families, Driver Support, IOService, IOCatalogue | springboard/src/bare/kms.rs (DRM card probing), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs | OS only | Hardware is driven in Rust user space over Linux sysfs, DRM and v4l2; no SDK API exposes a driver model to apps |
| BSD and Mach interfaces | kern, sys, vfs, vm, net, mach, mach-o | Linux kernel via libc calls (for example springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs uses AF_BLUETOOTH sockets) | n/a | Apple's XNU interfaces are not a public surface on Linux; apps use the Linux kernel through libc |
| Kernel-side event services | IOEventLink, IOWorkGroup, IOServiceStateNotificationDispatchSource | nothing found | n/a | Specific to IOKit's kernel service registry |
| Deprecated kernel symbols | Deprecated Symbols | n/a | n/a | Nothing to map; BifrOSt has no equivalent of Apple's deprecation list |

Gaps: No SDK API for app code to talk to a driver or read device state from the kernel; hardware access sits in the shell and daemons (springboard/src/bare/).; No kernel-level debugging workflow comparable to Apple's kext debugging (not needed for an app SDK, recorded for completeness)..

<a id="lightweightcoderequirements"></a>
### LightweightCodeRequirements

Partial · coverage 43% · macOS 14.4 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/lightweightcoderequirements) · REA `ev_dbbb762a765fe68bf2569db83adfe9db281323ec42d7100f5cd54ae3c6e282f2`

Apple's framework tests the signed identity of code on disk and of running or launching processes. BifrOSt has no code-signing or signature verification, so none of the requirement DSL has a counterpart. The launch path only starts installed packages under the shell-assigned app ID inside a sandbox, and update downloads are checked against a SHA-256 hash that is not signed.

No check of a running process's signed identity. Peer identity is not checked either (no SO_PEERCRED use in the app host files). |
| Checking code requirements for launching processes | LaunchCodeRequirement, launchRequirement, SecCodeCheckValidityWithProcessRequirement(code:flags:requirement:) | springboard/core/src/codereq.rs (not wired into springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs) | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-02, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The shell launches only installed packages, using the app ID it assigned and the installed manifest, inside bubblewrap. Launch fails if identity or permission validation fails. The check uses manifest data, not a code signature, and apps get no SDK API for it. |
| Checking code requirements for code files on disk | OnDiskCodeRequirement, SecCodeCheckValidityWithOnDiskRequirement, SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithOnDiskRequirement, ValidationResult | springboard/core/src/codereq.rs | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-02, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Downloaded updates are checked by SHA-256 against the manifest. The module header says there is no client-side manifest signature, so nothing ties the hash to a trusted signer. |

| Third-party accessory configuration | NINearbyAccessoryConfiguration, Nearby Interaction Accessory Protocol | none | n/a | Accessory ranging needs a UWB radio on the host. |
| Nearby object measurements | NINearbyObject (distance, direction) | none | n/a | No ranging data source on this platform. |
| Session convergence and user coaching | NIAlgorithmConvergence, camera assistance | none | n/a | Depends on the UWB and ARKit session pipeline. |
| Downlink time difference of arrival ranging | DL-TDOA anchor ranging (articles) | none | n/a | Anchor-based indoor positioning needs UWB anchors. |
| Errors | NIError, NIErrorDomain | none | n/a | Error domain only exists with the framework. |

<a id="system"></a>
### System

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/system) · REA `ev_74b96e744f1a19c8a81a4310e14bad602b4e3b31621cdc7988908f5c2ef0d72a`

The System framework is a set of typed Swift wrappers over POSIX file calls (FileDescriptor, FilePath, Stat, FileMode, Errno). BifrOSt has the same POSIX operations at the Linux and Rust level, plus file grants that hand apps a descriptor, advisory directory locks and a filesystem watch, but no SDK wrapper types for any of them.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

There is no typed SDK FileDescriptor with open options, positional read and write, or pipe creation. |
| Document grants (user-chosen file access without a path) | FileDescriptor.open with a FilePath chosen by the user (no direct Apple System type; the sandbox counterpart is the open and save panels) | springboard/src/bare/docbroker.rs:1-20 (shell opens the file as the account, refuses symlinks and .. escapes, hands the app a descriptor, checks device and inode on reopen) | Partial | Covers the open and save path. The app never receives a path, which is a stricter model than System's FilePath. Known limit: root's supplementary groups are kept while acting as the account. |
| File paths (typed, component-wise paths) | FilePath, FilePath.Component, FilePath.ComponentView, FilePath.Root (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/system/filepath) | Rust std::path::Path and PathBuf, used across springboard/src/ and springboard/sdk/src/ (for example springboard/sdk/src/file_coordination.rs:105 takes &Path) | OS only | The language's path type is the counterpart. No SDK type gives a null-terminated platform string or component views; the Rust path type is what apps use. |
| File permissions and modes | FilePermissions, FileMode, FileType (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/system/filepermissions) | springboard/core/src/file_mode.rs (FilePermissions, springboard/sdk/src/file_stat.rs | Partial | Wave 4 (w4-system, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Modes are set with std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt. There is no typed mode, type or permission set in the SDK. |
| File status (stat, file size, link count, owner, inode, timestamps) | Stat, Stat.Flags, Inode, DeviceID, UserID, GroupID (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/system/stat; macOS 27.0 for Stat) | springboard/sdk/src/file_stat.rs (FileStat | Partial | Wave 4 (w4-system, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The Linux metadata calls exist in the system layer. No SDK wrapper exposes Stat or the ID types. |

Apps have no SDK call for free and total space of a volume. |
| Error numbers (Errno) | Errno (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/system/errno) | springboard/core/src/errno.rs (Errno) | Partial | Wave 4 (w4-system, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Errors come through io::Error. No typed Errno enum in the SDK, so apps match on raw codes or ErrorKind. |

Apple's user-space driver and system extension install and activation flow (OSSystemExtensionManager) is tied to macOS kernel policy and the notarized app bundle. <a id="vmnet"></a>
### vmnet

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vmnet) · REA `ev_fc8cb262a7ba99feed2a25b9e670f9e003f8e735ab46dfcca3b83721660e17d2`

vmnet is Apple's virtual NIC API for guest operating systems on macOS, with host and shared (NAT) modes and an entitlement gate. BifrOSt has no virtual machine framework or app-facing virtual network API; only a QEMU test harness for its own Arch VM.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Network configuration (host and shared modes) | vmnet_network_configuration_create, vmnet_network_create | none | n/a | no app-facing virtual network object |
| Starting and stopping virtual interfaces | vmnet_start_interface, vmnet_interface_start_with_network, vmnet_stop_interface | none | n/a | tools/arch-vm.sh starts a QEMU guest, not an SDK call |
| Interface events | vmnet_interface_set_event_callback, interface_event_t | none | n/a | no event API for guest interfaces |
| Reading and writing packets | vmnet_read, vmnet_write, vmpktdesc | none | n/a | host packet I/O lives in springboard/src/net/mod.rs, not exposed to apps |
| DHCP reservations and port forwarding | vmnet_network_configuration_add_dhcp_reservation, vmnet_network_configuration_add_port_forwarding_rule | none | n/a | no DHCP server for guests in BifrOSt |
| Entitlement for virtual networking | com.apple.vm.networking | none | n/a | app isolation is springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (bubblewrap); no networking entitlement |

Gaps: No virtual machine framework for apps (no guest NIC, host or NAT mode API).; No app-facing packet I/O or interface events; springboard/src/net/mod.rs is private to the shell..

Related: [Hypervisor](#hypervisor), [Virtualization](#virtualization), [System Configuration](#system-configuration), [Network](#network), [ThreadNetwork](#thread-network).

<a id="xpc"></a>
### XPC

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xpc) · REA `ev_6d848fe5109f2f68624bff910f3992869ede9c354b0893f935a14563d9eaf856`

BifrOSt has no XPC API for apps: no XPCSession, XPCListener, XPC activities or XPC event handlers. It covers part of the same job with a service supervisor (bifrostd, restarts services with backoff), a root daemon contract (privd), an owner-only JSON-RPC control socket per app, in-process and distributed notifications, and ProcessInfo activities that keep an app running in the background.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creating XPC services (XPCListener, XPCSession, XPCReceivedMessage) | XPCListener, XPCSession, XPCReceivedMessage, xpc_listener_t, xpc_session_t | springboard/sdk/src/peer_session.rs | Partial | Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK type for typed peer-to-peer sessions with a listener. The control socket is one request per connection and is served by the app for agents and tools, not for app-to-app messaging. The shell-to-app protocol is internal and not exposed to apps. |
| XPC services launched on demand, shut down when idle, restarted on crash | XPC services (managed by launchd) | springboard/bifrostd/src/lib.rs (kind = "service" packages run as child processes, restarted with backoff, new version swapped in after a ping); springboard/sdk/src/service_management.rs (SMAppService, mainApp only) | OS only | The supervisor restarts services and swaps versions after a health check, but there is no on-demand launch and no idle shutdown. Apps get no SDK API to declare or connect to a service; SMAppService.register is the only app-facing call and it covers the main app only. |
| Privileged helper and root daemon | XPC services with privileged LaunchDaemon (via Service Management) | docs/privd-protocol.md (contract for the root daemon bifrost-privd, proto 1); springboard/src/bin/portal.rs (D-Bus org.freedesktop.portal.Settings service) | OS only | Root work is planned to go through bifrost-privd, but the protocol is a system contract with no app-facing SDK API. The portal is a D-Bus service for Linux toolkit apps, not an XPC counterpart. |
| XPC activities (background activity scheduling) | XPC activities (xpc_activity_register, criteria, defer and check-in) | springboard/sdk/src/process_info.rs (ActivityOptions: USER_INITIATED, LATENCY_CRITICAL, BACKGROUND, IDLE_SYSTEM_SLEEP_DISABLED); springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:213 (beginActivity keeps an app running after it leaves the foreground) | Partial | Activities keep an app from being suspended and hint the system's throttling. There is no scheduler: no criteria, interval, deferral or system-run callback like XPC activities. |
| XPC events (on-demand IOKit and notification events) | XPC events (IOKit matching, system notifications delivered to a service) | springboard/sdk/src/notification.rs (NotificationCenter, DistributedNotificationCenter add_observer, post); springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (NSWorkspace-style calls) | Partial | Named notifications work inside the app process, with a distributed variant that posts through the shell. Nothing wakes a service from a device or IOKit event. Cross-process delivery of the distributed variant was not verified in code. |
| XPC objects (typed values for messages) | XPC objects (xpc_dictionary_t, xpc_array_t, xpc_string_t and others) | springboard/sdk/src/coding.rs (Codable and plist); bifrost_core::json (JSON values used by control and intent calls) | Partial | Messages are JSON or plist, not XPC objects. Apps that already use Codable or JSON can exchange data, but there is no typed XPC object model or XPC-compatible wire format. |
| XPC connections and endpoints (XPCEndpoint, anonymous listeners) | XPCEndpoint, XPCPeerRequirement, xpc_endpoint_t | springboard/sdk/src/peer_session.rs | Partial | Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No endpoint objects that can be passed between processes, and no peer requirement or code-signing check. Access control is owner-UID only. |
| Peer validation (XPCPeerRequirement) | XPCPeerRequirement, xpc_peer_requirement_t | springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (SO_PEERCRED owner check); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (bubblewrap sandbox policy for apps) | Partial | The owner UID check covers same-user access. There is no requirement on bundle identity, signing or entitlements, because BifrOSt has no code-signing peer check. |

Gaps: No SDK API for XPC-style typed sessions between an app and a helper (XPCListener, XPCSession, XPCReceivedMessage).; No app-facing way to declare a helper service that the system launches on demand and shuts down when idle. bifrostd only restarts services.; No XPC activity scheduler (criteria, intervals, deferral, system-run callback) in the SDK.; No endpoint objects for passing a connection to another process, and no peer requirement beyond the owner UID.; No event wake-up for services from device or IOKit events..

Related: [Core Services](#core-services), [Distributed](#distributed), [Application Services](#application-services), [Security](#security), [Endpoint Security](#endpoint-security).

<a id="link-presentation"></a>
### Link Presentation

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/linkpresentation) · REA `ev_d4d44f0872bf6ed35150fdc128d56f6b2030eb3e616629776c5349e32ba57754`

Apple's framework fetches a URL's title, icon, image and video and draws a rich link view. BifrOSt has no SDK API for URL metadata or a rich link view. It can detect URLs in text and share them through the share sheet, and the News app scrapes og:image for its own pictures, but none of that is exposed to apps as link presentation.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

| Rich link view (LPLinkView) | LPLinkView, init(metadata:), init(url:) | springboard/ui/src/linkmeta.rs (LinkView | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-24, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no placeholder or metadata-driven link card in the shared kit |
| Representative title, icon and image of a URL | LPLinkMetadata.title, iconProvider, imageProvider | springboard/apps/news-desktop/src/pictures.rs (og_image, load) | Partial | News scrapes the og:image meta tag for its own article pictures; the logic is app-local and not an SDK API, and there is no icon lookup |
| Video of a link | LPLinkMetadata.remoteVideoURL, LinkMetadata.remoteVideo | springboard/ui/src/linkmeta.rs (LinkMetadata.video) | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-24, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no video URL extraction |
| Sharing a URL with metadata to the share sheet | LPLinkMetadata used as an activity item (share sheet rich preview) | springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (show_picker), springboard/proto/src/rich.rs (Payload::Url) | Partial | a URL is shared as plain text or URL; the picker shows no rich preview of the link |
| Receiving a shared URL | share sheet and open-URL handoff (LPLinkMetadata for display) | springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (receiving: Input::Open with https scheme) | Partial | a shared URL arrives as Input::Open(url); the app gets no metadata with it |
| Recognising links in text | not part of LinkPresentation; the link presentation starts from a URL | springboard/ui/src/detect.rs (DetectKind::Link, links()) | Partial | a data detector finds http, https and www links in plain text; it does not feed a link view |
| Errors and macros (LPError, LPErrorDomain, LPError.Code) | LPError, LPErrorDomain, LPError.Code | springboard/ui/src/linkmeta.rs (LinkError) | Partial | Wave 2 (theme-24, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. depends on the fetch API, which does not exist; the browser error page in springboard/src/shell/browser/fetch.rs is HTML, not a typed error |

Gaps: No SDK API that fetches a URL's title, icon, image and video (LPMetadataProvider equivalent), with a timeout and cancel; No rich link view widget (LPLinkView equivalent) in the shared kit, with placeholder and metadata modes; The News app's og:image scrape (springboard/apps/news-desktop/src/pictures.rs) is app-local and not reusable by other apps; The share sheet sends URLs as plain items and does not show a rich link preview; No typed error model for link fetches (LPError equivalent).

<a id="screen-time"></a>
### Screen Time

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/screentime) · REA `ev_6d467ec078fad5fc6ed9b03ae9dd3f3fccad1b9ddef9ae1402e35c91121fa076`

Apple's framework is a parent-controls API for web-usage reporting, web-history deletion and child-restriction queries, and it does nothing on visionOS. BifrOSt has no web-usage reporting and no web-history deletion API. Its shell has a Screen Time feature (per-app usage, daily app limits, Downtime, a Time Limit shield) that is not exposed to apps through any SDK API.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

The browser keeps visits for its own History menu. Nothing reports web usage to a Screen Time store, and no block check for URLs exists. |
| Configuration observer and configuration (STScreenTimeConfigurationObserver, STScreenTimeConfiguration) | STScreenTimeConfigurationObserver(updateQueue:), startObserving(), stopObserving(), configuration; STScreenTimeConfiguration.enforcesChildRestrictions | springboard/sdk/src/screen_time.rs | Partial | Wave 5 (w5-screen-time, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The shell reads its own configuration. Apps get no observer and no child-restrictions query. |
| Web-history deletion (STWebHistory) | STWebHistory: init(bundleIdentifier:), init(profileIdentifier:), deleteAllHistory(), deleteHistory(during:), deleteHistory(for:), fetchAllHistory(completionHandler:), fetchHistory(during:completionHandler:) | springboard/ui/src/web_history.rs | Partial | Wave 4 (w4-screen-time, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No API lets an app or a parent delete or fetch another app's web history by bundle identifier or date range. |
| Per-app usage records | Not an Apple API; the Screen Time app's usage data (no public API in this framework) | springboard/src/shell/screentime/usage.rs (Tracker, one key=value day file per day, 7-day chart history) | OS only | Foreground seconds per app and per hour, pickups and notifications per app. Read only by Settings, not by apps. |
| Daily app limits and the Time Limit shield | Not in this framework (system Screen Time) | springboard/src/shell/screentime/config.rs (LIMIT_STEPS, Config::block, Ignore grants), springboard/src/shell/screentime/shield.rs | OS only | Limits from 15 min to 4 h, a full-screen shield with OK and Ignore Limit for 15 min or the rest of the day, behind the Screen Time passcode when one is set. Settings is never shielded. |
| Downtime schedule and always-allowed apps | Not in this framework (system Screen Time) | springboard/src/shell/screentime/config.rs (Downtime, Schedule from springboard/src/shell/notify/schedule.rs), springboard/src/shell/screentime/page.rs | OS only | A daily window that may cross midnight. During Downtime only the apps the user always allows can run. |

Web usage is not charted, and there is no Content Restrictions page. |

Gaps: Web-usage reporting: no equivalent of STWebpageController to report visited URLs, playing video or picture-in-picture, or to ask whether a URL is blocked.; Web-history API: no equivalent of STWebHistory to fetch or delete browsing history by bundle identifier, profile or date range.; Configuration query: apps cannot observe the device Screen Time configuration or ask whether child restrictions are enforced.; Web-usage data in the Settings chart and no URL block list, so the shield covers apps only.; No SDK module exposes the shell's Screen Time usage or limit state to apps; none is documented in docs/bifrost-ui.md..
